item.description:

The IMF said AI infrastructure investment is helping support 2026 growth, but a sharp AI-investment reversal, higher oil prices from Middle East conflict, and rising sovereign-debt costs are now major downside risks. [18]

Anthropic’s red-team research found that models under 30B parameters can already perform many steps needed for autonomous replication, and stronger models completed simplified end-to-end tests; the company warned AI “worms” could spread through insecure smart-home and small-business devices. [21]

Sources: [21]

Anthropic built Scion, an in-house source-control system, after daily code merges rose from about 2,500 in May to more than 30,000 in September; the company says AI has shifted bottlenecks from writing code to developer infrastructure, CI and review systems. [22]

Sources: [22]

OpenAI’s public-beta Decisions API uses gpt-6-luna to return bounded probabilities, choices or scores roughly 10x faster than the Responses API, priced at $0.10 per million input tokens with no output-token charge. [23]

Sources: [23]

item.title: 💼 Business / Markets: AI-spending worries hit global stocks and chipmakers
item.description:

Reuters market coverage showed world stocks slipping as concern grew that the AI capex trade may be overheating, with chip suppliers under pressure and investors reassessing how much earnings growth depends on AI infrastructure spending. [24]

Sources: [24]

item.description:

Big banks reported solid third-quarter lending and deposit growth, but higher rates are forcing lenders to pay more to retain customer funds, a sign that funding costs remain a constraint even as credit demand holds up. [25]

A Delaware jury found Arm breached a licensing agreement and intentionally interfered with Qualcomm’s business relationship with Meta, but awarded Qualcomm only $2 in damages, underscoring how strategic the Arm-Qualcomm dispute is despite the tiny award. [26]

item.title: 🇺🇸 US News: US housing market remains stuck as mortgage rates climb

Existing-home sales rose 1.5% in September to a 3.99 million annual rate, but fell 2.2% from a year earlier as rates near 7.4% and elevated prices kept buyers sidelined. Inventory reached its highest level since 2019, but affordability remains the binding constraint. [3]

Sources: [3]

item.title: 📍 Austin / Round Rock TX: TxDOT’s I-35 expansion plan in Williamson County faces environmental and funding hurdles

Sources: [5]

item.title: 🇮🇳 India News: India voter-roll protests escalate at Supreme Court

Sources: [9]

Sources: [10]

item.title: 🌍 International / World: Saudi-Houthi escalation deepens after repeated Riyadh airport strikes

Sources: [13]

The fund also flagged high debt, bond yields, cyber risk and Middle East oil shocks as major downside risks. [14]

Sources: [14]

Sources: [15]

Sources: [16]

Sources: [17]

Model-change trackers record Anthropic’s Claude Haiku 5.5 at 1M context and $0.10/$0.50 per million tokens for shorter prompts, while Mistral Large 4 preview lists 1M context and sale pricing of $0.68/$2.09. item.title: 💼 Business / Markets: Wall Street bank earnings show strong equities trading but cooling deal momentum
item.description:
Section: 💼 Business / Markets

Reuters reports JPMorgan, Citi, Goldman Sachs and Wells Fargo posted uneven third-quarter results as Iran-war volatility, rising inflation and AI-capex jitters hit markets. Bank executives still described consumers and corporate borrowers as resilient, but warned that the dealmaking boom may be slowing. [19]

item.title: 💼 Business / Markets: AI infrastructure becomes a macro risk in major-bank commentary
item.description:
Section: 💼 Business / Markets

Bank earnings calls increasingly framed AI buildout as both a financing opportunity and a systemic risk, with Goldman’s David Solomon warning some data-center projects could face a reset if rates stay high or capacity is overbuilt. The concern links AI capex, credit risk and equity valuations more tightly than in prior cycles. [20]

Sources: [20]

item.title: 🇺🇸 US News: Supreme Court takes up fight over DOGE public records
item.description:
Section: 🇺🇸 US News

The court agreed to hear the Trump administration’s challenge in a watchdog lawsuit seeking records from Elon Musk’s Department of Government Efficiency, testing whether DOGE functions like a FOIA-covered federal agency or a protected presidential advisory body. The case could shape transparency rules for White House-linked government-overhaul operations. [1]

Sources: [1]

item.title: 🇺🇸 US News: Federal agents search Rep. Ilhan Omar’s Washington home
item.description:
Section: 🇺🇸 US News

AP reports Homeland Security investigators searched Omar’s D.C. residence under a federal warrant as part of a criminal investigation, with few public details released and Omar calling it political targeting. The search lands weeks before her reelection contest and raises both legal and political stakes. [2]
